title: Time and Calendars
intro: Seconds, days, months and years: how well do you know the clock and the calendar?

questions.prompt: How many months of the year have 31 days?
questions.explanation: January, March, May, July, August, October and December each have 31 days: seven months in all.

questions.prompt: How many hours are there in one day?
questions.explanation: A whole day, from one midnight to the next, lasts 24 hours.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in a year that is not a leap year?
questions.explanation: An ordinary year has 365 days. Every fourth year or so is a leap year with 366.

questions.prompt: In a leap year, February has 29 days.
questions.explanation: February usually has 28 days, but in a leap year it gets an extra day and has 29.

questions.prompt: How many seconds are there in one minute?
questions.explanation: One minute is made of 60 seconds, and one hour is made of 60 minutes.

questions.prompt: Which month comes straight after June?
questions.explanation: The months run January, February, March, April, May, June, July and so on, so July follows June.

questions.prompt: A decade is 100 years long.
questions.explanation: A decade is 10 years. A period of 100 years is called a century.

questions.prompt: Roughly how long does Earth take to travel once around the Sun?
questions.explanation: Earth takes about 365 days, one year, to orbit the Sun. Its spin on its own axis gives us day and night.

questions.prompt: How many weeks are there in a year, to the nearest whole number?
questions.explanation: A year of 365 days is 52 weeks and 1 day, so there are about 52 weeks in a year.

questions.prompt: In the UK, the longest day of the year falls in which month?
questions.explanation: The longest day, called the summer solstice, is around 21 June. After that, the days slowly start getting shorter again.

questions.prompt: How many years are there in a century?
questions.explanation: A century is 100 years. The word comes from 'centum', the Latin for one hundred, just like 'cent' and 'centimetre'.

questions.prompt: What do we call a period of 1,000 years?
questions.explanation: A millennium is 1,000 years. The year 2000 was a big celebration because a new millennium was about to begin.

questions.prompt: How many seconds are there in one hour?
questions.explanation: There are 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour. 60 lots of 60 makes 3,600 seconds.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in September?
questions.explanation: September has 30 days. The rhyme 'Thirty days has September, April, June and November' helps you remember.

questions.prompt: In the UK, which season comes straight after summer?
questions.explanation: The four seasons go spring, summer, autumn and winter. In autumn, many trees drop their leaves.

questions.prompt: On a 24-hour clock, how is 3 o'clock in the afternoon written?
questions.explanation: On a 24-hour clock you keep counting after midday, so 1 pm is 13:00, 2 pm is 14:00 and 3 pm is 15:00.

questions.prompt: What does 'am' after a time tell you?

options.label: It is between midnight and midday
It is between midday and midnight

questions.explanation: 'am' means the morning half of the day, from midnight until midday. 'pm' is used from midday until midnight.

questions.prompt: On a clock with hands, what does the short hand show?
questions.explanation: The short hand points to the hour and the long hand points to the minutes.

questions.prompt: How many minutes are there in a quarter of an hour?
questions.explanation: An hour has 60 minutes. One quarter of 60 is 15, so a quarter of an hour is 15 minutes.

questions.prompt: How many days are there in a fortnight?
questions.explanation: A fortnight is two weeks. Two lots of seven days makes 14 days.

questions.prompt: If today is Monday, what day will it be in three days' time?
questions.explanation: Count on from Monday: Tuesday is one day, Wednesday is two and Thursday is three.

questions.prompt: Leap years usually come around once every how many years?
questions.explanation: A leap year usually happens every four years, when an extra day is added to the end of February.

questions.prompt: How many hours are there from midday to midnight?
questions.explanation: Midday is 12 noon and midnight is 12 hours later. A whole day, from midnight to midnight, is 24 hours.

questions.prompt: What causes day and night on Earth?
questions.explanation: Earth spins once about every 24 hours. The side facing the Sun has day, and the side facing away has night.

questions.prompt: The 'G' in GMT, the time used in the UK in winter, stands for which place?
questions.explanation: GMT stands for Greenwich Mean Time. It is measured from the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London.

questions.prompt: April has 31 days.
questions.explanation: April has only 30 days. It is one of the four months, with June, September and November, that have 30 days.

questions.prompt: On a 24-hour clock, midnight can be written as 00:00.
questions.explanation: At midnight the 24-hour clock starts again from zero, so midnight is written 00:00.

questions.prompt: The year 2000 was a leap year.
questions.explanation: Years that end in 00 are only leap years if they can be divided by 400. 2000 can, so it had a 29 February.

questions.prompt: From one full moon to the next takes about how many days?
questions.explanation: The Moon takes about 29 and a half days to go through all its phases, from full moon back to full moon. That is where the idea of a month comes from.

questions.prompt: How many minutes are there in one whole day?
questions.explanation: There are 60 minutes in an hour and 24 hours in a day. 24 lots of 60 makes 1,440 minutes.
